<p style="font-size:14px;">
The Alder Flycatcher (*Empidonax alnorum*) is a migratory songbird associated with dense, early-successional vegetation and wet habitats, including shrub swamps, riparian areas, and regenerating forest openings. In the boreal region, the species benefits from naturally occurring disturbances such as fire and flooding that maintain young forest and shrub-dominated habitats. However, changes in disturbance regimes, habitat conversion, and alterations to wetland and riparian ecosystems may influence the availability and quality of suitable breeding habitat. Vulnerability assessments for this species consider factors such as habitat loss, landscape disturbance, and changes in habitat conditions across its breeding range.
</p>
